result.rationale: The diff assigns `destinationCalendar: ... : null` when neither eventType nor organizerUser has a destination calendar, then calls `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` only if isTeamEventType && COLLECTIVE. With optional chaining, a null destinationCalendar silently skips the push, discarding member destination calendars collected in teamDestinationCalendars, so those members' calendars are ignored with no error. This is a concrete, verifiable null-hole introduced by this diff.

judged_text: `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is a silent no-op when evt.destinationCalendar is null (the value the ternary above assigns when neither eventType nor organizerUser has a destination calendar), discarding the teamDestinationCalendars just collected. A COLLECTIVE event type where the organizer has no destination calendar but team members do skips all member destination calendars from the event-creation path; team members' configured calendars are silently ignored with no error or log, and the next person to touch collective calendar routing has to rediscover this null-hole.

adjudication.rationale: In `handleNewBooking.ts`, `evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists (`: null` in the ternary). Immediately after, for COLLECTIVE team events the code does `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`, which becomes a silent no-op when `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`. Since `teamDestinationCalendars` are collected from team members’ `user.destinationCalendar`, this path drops them entirely, and downstream `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` only iterates when `event.destinationCalendar && event.destinationCalendar.length > 0`, so those member calendars will be ignored.
